reasoning_traces.think:
TextGrad introduces a formalism for optimizing complex AI systems composed of multiple LLM calls. The core abstraction mirrors PyTorch autograd: Variables track values and dependencies, Forward computes outputs from inputs, Backward generates textual gradients, and TGD performs updates. These primitives enable joint optimization of prompts and code in GSE pipelines. The method assumes that textual gradients approximate true derivatives and that a shared backward engine works across domains. Failure modes include hallucinations in backward engine feedback, overfitting due to LLM-judged losses, and lack of convergence guarantees. In GSI, this framework supports Bayesian inference by treating textual variables as latent states in probabilistic models. In GSE, it enables iterative refinement of agent behavior through deterministic backtests, avoiding reliance on potentially biased LLM evaluators.
